tasks.short: Walk the plant round checking for leaks, noises and smells, read local gauges, tick the round checklist, and report leaks or malfunctions to the control room.

steps.what: Chemical operator patrols work areas to detect leaks, noises and smells
Chemical operator reads local gauges on the round
Chemical operator ticks the round checklist on paper
Chemical operator reports leaks and malfunctions to the control room by radio

tasks.design: Wireless transmitters on local gauges send readings to the control system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so fewer gauges need reading by eye on the round. The round checklist runs on an intrinsically safe handheld with a tag scan at each checkpoint and photos for findings. Patrolling and reporting leaks by radio stay with the operator; round logs are kept per round, not used to rate operators.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every local gauge was read by eye and the round ticked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Wireless gauge transmitters and safe handhelds are common in process plants.
tasks.still_hard: Leaks are found by smell and sound, which sensors cover poorly.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a pump bearing start to fail on the round.

reach.learn: Whether wireless readings show drifts sooner.

evidence.claim: Wireless transmitters can send local gauge readings to a plant control system.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems can monitor staff, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the round route to the malfunction report; repairs are outside.
Input contract: round routes set by the shift supervisor; gauge readings from transmitters where fitted; fallback is reading by eye.
Patrolling and reporting do not change.
Handhelds are certified for the plant's hazardous zones.

incremental.description: Chemical operator reports dead transmitters and missing tags.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few gauges fitted with transmitters; high: most local gauges transmit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch pressures, temperatures and flows on the control screens, take product samples, adjust setpoints to keep conditions in limits, and compare readings with the batch specification.

steps.what: Chemical operator monitors recording instruments and flowmeters on the control screens
Chemical operator compares readings with the paper batch specification sheet
Chemical operator takes product samples and checks their appearance
Chemical operator adjusts setpoints so specified conditions are maintained

tasks.design: Specification limits for each batch are loaded into the control system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) from the recipe, and control charts with alarms show when pressure, temperature or flow drifts toward a limit, so readings are not compared with paper sheets. Sampling and adjusting setpoints stay with the operator; no setpoint changes automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were compared by eye with the batch sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC software reads instruments and PLCs and shows control charts with alarms.
tasks.still_hard: Too many alarms bury the important ones.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a slow drift means a fouling heat exchanger.
tasks.altitude: The operator answers flagged drifts instead of scanning every value.

reach.learn: Whether drift alarms cut off-spec batches.

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs and shows control charts and alarms.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from process data to conditions held; maintenance is outside.
Input contract: specification limits from the recipe set by the process engineer; fallback is the paper sheet.
Sampling and adjusting do not change.
Alarm limits are reviewed so alarms stay few.

incremental.description: Chemical operator reports nuisance alarms to the process engineer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older units with few recorded instruments; high: units fully on the control system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write hourly temperatures and pressures, record ingredients and lot numbers, enter lab results, note processing times and deviations, check the batch record and send it to quality assurance.

steps.what: Chemical operator records temperatures and pressures in the shift log every hour
Chemical operator records ingredients used and their lot numbers
Chemical operator enters lab test results in the batch record
Chemical operator notes processing times and deviations
Chemical operator checks the batch record is complete at the end of the shift
Chemical operator hands the batch record to quality assurance

tasks.design: The process historian ({OPS_SYSTEM}) logs temperatures, pressures and processing times, so hourly readings are not written down. Lot barcodes are scanned and weights read from the scale when materials are charged, and lab results flow from the lab system into the electronic batch record. The operator writes deviation reasons, checks the record for flagged gaps, and once checked the record goes to quality assurance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings, lots, times and lab results were written in paper logs and batch sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Historians, scanners and lab system links fill electronic batch records.
tasks.still_hard: Deviation reasons still need the operator's words.
tasks.human_edge: Writing down why a batch behaved oddly so the next shift understands.
tasks.altitude: The operator checks and explains the record instead of writing it.

reach.learn: Whether complete records speed up release.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing's MES computes recipe parameters by business rules and captures SPC and defect data.
Per-operator logs in shop-floor systems need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from process data to the record with quality assurance; batch release is outside.
Input contract: process data from the historian; lab results from the lab system; lot labels from suppliers; fallback is paper logs.
Deviation reasons and the final check stay with the operator.
The record is kept per batch, not used to rate operators.
research_questions: Are batch records complete at first check?

already_counted.description: Chemical operator reviews flagged gaps in the batch record.

incremental.description: Chemical operator enters values when a link fails.

approvals.approved_version: The batch record as checked complete by the operator in s5; later changes need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older units without historian or scale links; high: units fully linked to historian, scales and lab system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the production plan, calculate raw material quantities, check tank levels and warehouse stock, decide what to request, and request materials from the warehouse.

steps.what: Chemical operator reads the production plan for the coming shifts
Chemical operator estimates materials required from recipes and batch sizes
Chemical operator checks tank levels and warehouse stock
Chemical operator decides what to request and when
Chemical operator requests materials from the warehouse

tasks.design: The production plan in the MES ({OPS_SYSTEM}) multiplies recipe quantities by planned batch sizes, and tank level sensors and warehouse stock from the ERP ({ERP}) show what is on hand next to the needs. The operator decides what to request and when, and the request goes to the warehouse from the same screen. Deciding stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantities were calculated in a spreadsheet, tanks dipped or read on site, and requests phoned in.
tasks.enabler_now: MES and ERP systems compute material needs from recipes and show stock and tank levels.
tasks.still_hard: Rush orders and rework batches change needs at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a supplier's lot runs thin and asking for extra early.
tasks.altitude: The operator decides requests from ready figures instead of calculating them.

reach.learn: Whether requests arrive earlier and more complete.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing's MES computes recipe parameters by business rules.
No Annex III point of the AI Act fits material estimates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the production plan to the material request; buying from suppliers is outside.
Input contract: production plan from the planner; recipes from the process engineer; stock from the ERP; fallback is spreadsheet and phone.
Deciding requests stays with the operator.
Warehouse staff time is outside the operator's savings.
research_questions: Do material shortages during batches fall?

incremental.description: Chemical operator reports wrong tank readings.

approvals.approved_version: The quantities and timing as decided by the operator in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tanks without level sensors and recipes outside the MES; high: all tanks and recipes in the systems.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chemical operator keeps patrols, sampling, setpoints and decisions; reading gauges by eye, paper logs and spreadsheet sums shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator who spends saved time on the plant floor finding problems early.
